column3: “For desire he seeks” is rendered “seeks his own desire,” and “bursts out” as “quarrels.” The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “Its heart” is rendered “his own mind.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists “a flowing wadi, a fountain of wisdom”; NASB makes it a sentence, “The fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.”
Close to the Hebrew; “To lift up the face” is rendered “To show partiality.”
Close to the Hebrew; “They go in strife” is rendered “bring strife.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “A slanderer” is rendered “a whisperer,” and “the chambers of the belly” as “the innermost parts of the body.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A master of destruction” is rendered “him who destroys.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He is set on high” is rendered “is safe.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The town of his strength” is rendered “his strong city.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “Brings back a word” is rendered “gives an answer.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Stricken” is rendered “broken.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A discerning heart” is rendered “The mind of the prudent.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “seems” and “Until another comes.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Separates” is rendered “decides.”
NASB adds “is harder to be won”; the Hebrew says “a brother transgressed [is] more than a strong city.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “In the hand of the tongue” is rendered “in the power of the tongue.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He finds a wife” is rendered “He who finds a wife,” and “pleasure” as “favor.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Strong [words]” is rendered “roughly.”
“A person of companions [is] to be broken” is rendered “A man of many friends comes to ruin,” and “one who loves” as “a friend.”
